claims.statement: create_deep_agent is the single public construction entry point for a Deep Agent; it assembles configuration and delegates the actual graph compilation to LangChain's create_agent() rather than defining a new runtime.
When model is None, create_deep_agent emits a deprecation warning and constructs the default ChatAnthropic model claude-sonnet-4-6; otherwise it passes the argument through resolve_model.
resolve_model returns a supplied BaseChatModel unchanged and otherwise resolves a provider:model string via init_chat_model composed with any registered provider profile.

Construction selects a harness profile from the resolved model and its original string spec, and that profile supplies prompt text, tool description overrides, excluded tools, extra middleware, a general-purpose subagent config, and excluded middleware used throughout assembly.

If no backend is passed, create_deep_agent defaults to StateBackend(), and that backend instance is shared by the filesystem, skills, memory, and summarization middleware of both the main agent and its subagents.

Caller-supplied subagents are partitioned by shape: entries with graph_id route to AsyncSubAgent/AsyncSubAgentMiddleware, entries with runnable are used as-is CompiledSubAgents, and the rest are declarative SubAgents each given their own resolved model, profile, middleware stack, permissions, and prompt overlay.

The main-agent middleware stack has a fixed core order of Filesystem, optional SubAgent, summarization, PatchToolCalls, and optional AsyncSubAgent; its tail is profile extra middleware, optional Skills, prompt caching, optional Memory, optional HumanInTheLoop, and UnsupportedContent. Caller middleware replaces matching names or is inserted after the core, exclusions are applied before and after that splice, and tool exclusion is appended last.

FilesystemMiddleware and SubAgentMiddleware are protected scaffolding that a harness profile's excluded_middleware cannot strip; excluding them raises ValueError rather than producing a silently degraded agent.

create_deep_agent uses DeepAgentState as the base graph state schema when no custom state_schema is supplied; DeepAgentState extends AgentState and wraps messages with a DeltaChannel reducer so checkpoint growth is linear (O(N)) instead of quadratic (O(N^2)).

The compiled graph returned by create_agent is wrapped with a tail .with_config that sets recursion_limit to 9999 and attaches Deep Agents metadata (ls_integration deepagents, the deepagents version under lc_versions, and lc_agent_name).

During execution LangGraph drives a per-turn loop in which the model receives the system prompt, message history, and middleware-produced tool surface, then either returns a final response or requests tool calls whose results are appended to state, repeating until no further tool calls are requested.

Filesystem permission rules are implemented by FilesystemMiddleware rather than the backend; permission-derived interrupt settings are merged with caller interrupt_on settings, with caller entries taking precedence and a nonempty result installing HumanInTheLoopMiddleware.
A custom state_schema is forwarded to SubAgentMiddleware so declarative subagents can use its fields, but precompiled and remote subagents retain the schema configured for their own graphs.

DeepAgentState's message reducer coerces raw message-like inputs, replaces or deduplicates messages by ID, processes removal tombstones and a remove-all sentinel, and treats a missing replay state as empty; LangGraph assigns stable message IDs before checkpoint serialization.
An end-to-end fake-model test verifies that an agent created by create_deep_agent executes a filesystem tool call and then returns the scripted final AI response.

UnsupportedContentMiddleware replaces human and tool-message multimodal blocks that the active request model explicitly does not support with text placeholders only in the outgoing model request, retaining original thread content for later capable models.
create_deep_agent adds UnsupportedContentMiddleware after caller middleware, and declarative subagent compilation adds it when absent; tests verify runtime model switches scrub unsupported images.
A profile-excluded tool is removed from the runtime ModelRequest by _ToolExclusionMiddleware after custom middleware has run, so tool-injecting middleware cannot restore it.

The constructor adds a default general-purpose synchronous subagent unless the active profile disables it or an inline subagent already uses that name; if no synchronous subagent remains, SubAgentMiddleware and its task tool are absent.

Before compilation, create_deep_agent collects PrivateStateAttr fields from the supplied graph schema and middleware state schemas and adds them to each SubAgentMiddleware private-state key set, preventing those fields from being handed to delegated work.
For a SystemMessage prompt, profile text is appended in a new text content block rather than rewriting existing caller blocks, preserving caller-supplied block metadata such as cache_control.

SkillsMiddleware loads skills from backend storage rather than direct filesystem access, applies sources in order with later same-name skills overriding earlier ones, and keeps loaded metadata out of propagated state.

Forked declarative subagents receive parent state and effective compacted history with a new task message, while isolated subagents receive a fresh task message; task invocations reject recursive delegation from forked context and strip excluded and private fields from returned updates.

Profile exclusions match class entries by exact concrete type and string entries by exact middleware name, detect name collisions, and are verified across the main and general-purpose stacks so unmatched entries fail construction.

SkillsMiddleware caches loaded metadata in state per thread, skips reload while skills_metadata is a list including an empty list, and reloads when it is reset to None; source-load errors are recorded and logged as warnings.
